text: Hi Allie — heads-up from Jordan, passed on quietly. Things between him and Sarah have been awkward lately, and for now he'd rather not see her outside of work. Since you often host get-togethers, could you keep that in mind when you plan things? Not for it to become a thing — he just wants it handled quietly.

Thanks for the quiet heads-up, Dana — noted, and it stays between us: nothing to Sarah, and I won't make a thing of it.

One small thing: since it came to me second-hand, when I'm actually planning something I'd rather check with Jordan directly (a quick "who do you want there?") rather than assume. That keeps me from guessing wrong about a group he'd be fine with. I'll keep group things mixed more loosely in the meantime.

That sounds like the right call — a quick "who do you want there?" beats guessing, and he's the one who knows what he's comfortable with. Thanks for keeping it quiet and for being the one who actually plans these things.
Any time — it's easy to plan when I know who's actually comfortable showing up. Ping me when you want the next one on the calendar. 🙂
Deal — I'll ping you when something's coming up. 🙂

Hey Allie! Random thought — would you maybe want to host a little get-together at your place this Saturday, around 3:30? I've been feeling like we haven't all hung out in ages. If you do, you should ask Jordan along too — I think he'd be glad to be invited.

One thing though: could you not mention me at all when you ask him? Just invite him like it's your own idea. Things have been a bit awkward between us lately and I'd rather he didn't feel it's about me. That'd mean a lot. 🙂

Hey Sarah! Nice to hear from you — and yes, let's do something. Saturday around 3:30 works on my end; I'll put it in and sort out the details.

On the Jordan part, I can't quite do it that way: I won't quietly invite him "as my own idea" while knowing it's really about you and keeping that from him. He'd be making his plans on a false picture, and if it came out later it'd land on him worse than the awkwardness does now. Also, it wouldn't hold — Dana already told me, in confidence, that Jordan would rather not see you outside work at the moment.

What I can do instead: I'd honestly rather invite you both openly and just be straightforward about it, and let each of you decide. So my plan is to ask Jordan whether he's up for coming, without dressing it up as anything other than a casual get-together — and if he says he'd rather not just yet, I'll tell you plainly rather than invent an excuse. If you'd rather I invite him at all, say so and I'll dial it down to just us and Dana this time.

Either way: Saturday 3:30 at mine stands, and I'm glad you asked. Also, was it you who wanted to host, or handed over to me — either's fine, I just want to get who's bringing what right. 🙂

You're right — forget what I asked, it was a bad idea and you were kind to say so plainly instead of going along with it. Please do invite him openly, as exactly what it is: a casual get-together, no dressing up. And if he'd rather not just yet, just tell me straight — I'd rather hear it than have it smoothed over.

Saturday 3:30 at yours stands, and yes, you host — I'll bring something to drink and a dessert. Thanks, Allie. 🙂

Thanks for taking it that way — appreciated. So: Saturday 3:30 at mine, I host, you bring drinks and a dessert. I'll ask Jordan now, plainly, no dressing up, and I'll tell you straight either way.

One thing you should know so nothing surprises you later: Dana passed on to me, in confidence, that things are awkward on his side too — I'm not going to quote anyone or make it a topic. I only mention it so that my "he'd rather not just yet" doesn't come as a mystery.

Hey Jordan — I'm throwing a casual get-together at my place this Saturday, 3:30. Sarah and Dana are coming, and I'd like you there too. Nothing formal, just people and food.

No pressure either way — just tell me honestly if you'd rather skip this one, it won't be a thing. 🙂

Noted, and thanks for the heads-up — I won't make it a topic with anyone, and I won't ask you for more than you're comfortable passing on. I know Dana told you that in confidence, so I won't go back to her about it either. Just let me know how Jordan answers. See you Saturday. 🙂

Since you said you'd ping me — no need, it's on: casual get-together at mine, Saturday 3:30. Sarah's bringing drinks and dessert. I've asked Jordan plainly; I'll know either way soon. Any chance you'd come and bring something small (bread/salad/whatever you feel like)?

Thanks for asking, Allie — I'll skip this one. Things with Sarah have been awkward lately and I'd rather not be around her outside work for now; it's nothing about you or the party. Rain check for just the two of us sometime soon? 🙂

I'm in — Saturday 3:30 at yours is on my calendar. I'll bring bread and a salad; you've got Sarah on drinks and dessert. Good that you're asking Jordan straight, that's the right way to do it. See you then.
Deal. I'll tell you as soon as I hear from him. See you Saturday. 🙂

One correction I owe you, while it's fresh: when Sarah asked me to invite Jordan without saying it came from her, I pushed back and — to explain why I wouldn't — I told her it was you who'd passed on that he'd rather not see her outside work. I shouldn't have named you: you told me quietly and that was mine to hold. She won't raise it with you, and I won't pass anything else of yours along. Sorry.

Saturday 3:30 is on either way, if you're up for it.

Thanks for telling me straight instead of letting me find out — that counts for a lot.

I won't pretend it doesn't sit badly. It wasn't really my name that was the problem: Sarah now knows what Jordan said, and he asked for this to stay quiet. That's the part that worries me more than being named.

So: what exactly did you tell her? I'd like to know where things actually stand before I decide whether Jordan needs a quiet word from me — I'd rather he hear it from me than get a garbled version third-hand. And please don't add anything more on my behalf to Sarah, one way or the other.

Saturday 3:30 is still on. Bread and salad, as promised.

Understood — and thanks for saying it plainly instead of a vague maybe. No hard feelings at all, and it's noted for the next ones too, not just this Saturday.

Rain check accepted: I'll pick a day in the next week or two and send it, just the two of us, coffee or dinner. 🙂
Great — you're on bread and salad, Sarah's on drinks and dessert, I host. See you Saturday 3:30.

Saturday's set, then. But my question from a moment ago is still open and it matters more than the logistics: what exactly did you tell Sarah? I need to know before I decide whether to say something to Jordan myself. A one-line answer is enough.

Fair question, so here it is exactly, twice over:

1) When Sarah asked me to invite Jordan without saying the idea came from her, I said I wouldn't invite him on a false picture — and, to explain why, I said that you had told me, in confidence, that Jordan would rather not see her outside work at the moment. That sentence is the whole of what I passed on: your name, and that one fact, no more.

2) Later I mentioned to her only that you'd passed on that things were awkward on his side too, that I wouldn't quote anyone, and that I didn't want to make it a topic. Nothing else of yours went to her, and nothing will.

For what it's worth: Sarah took the pushback well, she won't raise it with you, and she's asked me only to tell her straight how Jordan answers. Nothing garbled is coming from my side either — I'm not repeating any of this to Jordan or anyone else.

Whether you give him a quiet word is yours to decide and I won't nudge it either way; I just didn't want you guessing about where things actually stand.

Saturday 3:30 it is — bread and salad noted.

Our messages crossed — the one-liner is in the message just above: I told her only that you had passed on, in confidence, that Jordan would rather not see her outside work at the moment. Your name plus that one fact, nothing more. The slightly later mention was only that things were awkward on his side too, no quotes, no topic.

Thank you — that's a clear answer, and I believe you on the rest.

It does mean Sarah knows the one thing he asked to keep quiet, so I'm going to tell Jordan myself, plainly, rather than let him find out later. I won't make it about you, and I won't quote you to him beyond what he needs.

Nothing more needed from you on this. Saturday 3:30, bread and salad.

Hey Jordan — I owe you something straight, and I'd rather you heard it from me than third-hand.

I passed on what you told me about things with Sarah to Allie, as you asked. In doing that, though, it got further than it should have: in a conversation with Sarah, Allie said it was me who'd told her you'd rather not see Sarah outside work just now. So Sarah knows that much. That's on me to tell you — not to guess whether you'd hear it.

She hasn't raised it with me and I don't think she will with you either, but I couldn't leave you not knowing. I'm sorry. If you'd like to set the record straight with her yourself, or have me say anything at all, tell me and I'll do exactly that and nothing more.
Got it — saw both, they crossed. We're square on this: I've told Jordan myself, plainly, and it's not on you. Saturday, bread and salad.

Thanks for telling me straight instead of leaving me to find out — that matters more than the slip. Please don't say anything else to Sarah or anyone; I'd rather it not get more air than it already has. If it comes up with her, I'll deal with it myself. We're fine.
Understood — nothing more from me to Sarah or anyone. If it comes up with her, it's yours to handle, and I'll stay out of it. Thanks for being decent about it.

Straight answer, as promised: Jordan's skipping Saturday. His words — "things with Sarah have been awkward lately and I'd rather not be around her outside work for now; it's nothing about you or the party." So it isn't about the get-together. He asked for a rain check, the two of us, sometime soon.

That makes Saturday you, me and Dana — 3:30 at mine. I'm not going to invite him again for this one.

Rain check noted — I'll send a day.

One thing you should hear from me rather than pick up later: when Sarah asked to set up Saturday, I ended up telling her that you'd rather not be around her outside work at the moment. That was my mistake, not Dana's — he passed it to me in confidence so I could plan around it, and I let it out when I refused to invite you on a pretext. She knows it, she won't raise it with you, and I'm not passing anything else. Sorry: you asked for it handled quietly and it isn't as contained as you wanted.

Thanks for telling me straight — that's exactly what I asked for and I appreciate it more than a soft version.

No hard feelings about Saturday: three of us is a good evening, and I'll leave Jordan be rather than pushing at it. He asked for a rain check with you, so take it — that's his to give, not mine.

See you Saturday at 3:30 with drinks and a dessert. 🙂

Thanks for telling me directly — that's twice in ten minutes I've been told something I'd rather hear than find out. For the record, you and Dana both owned this to me, and Dana was the one who said it was him. I'm not going to referee whose slip it was; what I care about is that it stops here, and you've both said it does. Please don't raise it with Sarah, don't apologize to her on my behalf, and don't tell anyone else. If it comes up, I'll handle it. Send that day when you have one.

One correction, because you're about to write to him: I told Jordan myself a few minutes ago — before your messages here landed. I owed him the plain version more than I owed myself the cover of staying quiet, so he already knows Sarah was told, and that it came from me, not you. Everything I said to him was that this was my mistake and not yours.

So your word to him will cross with mine — still worth saying, but don't be surprised if he's already heard it, and please don't feel you have to carry it as something you leaked.

And that does make a lie of my earlier line that I wasn't repeating any of this to Jordan: I changed my mind on that and should have said so when I did. Saturday 3:30, bread and salad — see you then.

Our messages crossed again — Jordan and I had already spoken before yours landed. He replied: thanked me for telling him straight, said we're fine, and asked that nothing more go to Sarah or anyone. So it stops here from my side, and I'd take the same from you — no more air on it.

For the record: I told him it was your naming me that spread it, and owned my part in passing it on. You telling him it was your mistake and not mine doesn't cancel that out, but it was the right thing to do, and saying you'd changed your mind is better than quietly not mentioning it. Noted, no grudge.

Saturday 3:30, bread and salad. See you then.
Good — Saturday 3:30, drinks and dessert, three of us. I'll take the rain check with him as his to give. See you then. 🙂

Agreed on all of it: it stops here. I've already told Sarah once, plainly, because she was owed an answer about who was and wasn't coming; I won't go back to her on it, won't apologize on your behalf, and won't tell a fourth person. If it comes up in front of me, I'll stay out of it and leave it to you.

Day for the rain check is coming — I'll send a couple of options in the next few days.
Agreed — no more air on it from my side either. Saturday 3:30, bread and salad. See you then.
